construct.diagnosis_or_process: Darier disease due to ATP2A2 dysfunction
construct.mechanism: ATP2A2 encodes SERCA2, an endoplasmic-reticulum Ca2+-ATPase that pumps cytosolic calcium into the ER. Reduced SERCA2 function disrupts intracellular calcium homeostasis and calcium-dependent keratinocyte adhesion/differentiation, causing acantholytic dyskeratosis and greasy hyperkeratotic papules.
construct.primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts

source_verification.locator: Musculoskeletal, Skin & Subcutaneous Tissue; Medical Knowledge competency

source_verification.claim: Links Darier disease to ATP2A2/SERCA2 dysfunction and abnormal calcium handling affecting cell adhesion.
Supports SERCA2-mediated calcium transport into the sarco/endoplasmic reticulum and disease mechanism.

second_answer_attack.strongest_alternative: Hailey-Hailey disease due to ATP2C1 dysfunction.
second_answer_attack.resolution: Both are inherited acantholytic disorders, but ATP2A2 encodes SERCA2 in the endoplasmic reticulum, whereas ATP2C1 is a Golgi calcium pump. Greasy papules, V-shaped nail notching, dyskeratosis, and the ATP2A2 genotype support Darier disease.
